chunks: 844 - Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:

"Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made the Ka'bah the qiblah for the people of the mosque, and He made the mosque the qiblah for the people of the Haram, and He made the Haram the qiblah for the people of the world."

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the world, meaning people outside the Haram
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary surrounding the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: the Ka'bah, the central sacred structure serving as qiblah
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, here referring to al-Masjid al-Haram

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describe the qiblah for people in different locations?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the graded orientation of the qiblah: the Ka'bah for those in the mosque, the mosque for those in the Haram, and the Haram for the rest of the world. It expresses a legal and devotional framework for determining the direction of salat (prayer) based on one's location.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.844 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said :

"Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, made the Ka’ba the Qiblah (direction of prayer) for the people of the mosque (Masjid al-Haram), and He made the mosque the Qiblah for the people of the sanctuary (Haram), and He made the sanctuary the Qiblah for the people of the world."
